newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi committal hearing opens in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi committal hearing opens in Milan.

text.p: A committal hearing opened on Tuesday to decide whether media tycoon Silvio Berlusconi should stand trial for allegedly establishing an illegal slush fund when his Fininvest company bought a film business in 1988.

Berlusconi, who served as prime minister for seven months in 1994 and leads Italy's centre-right Freedom Alliance, and four others are accused by Milan magistrate Margherita Taddei of falsifying company accounts and embezzling funds.

Taddei accuses the five men of paying more for the purchase of film company Medusa than the 28 billion lira that was written down in Fininvest's balance sheet. The extra amount was believed to have been used to establish a slush fund.
The other four men, all close business associates of Berlusconi, are Adriano Galliani, Giancarlo Foscale, Carlo Bernasconi and Livio Gironi.

Berlusconi, already on trial in Milan on charges of bribing tax inspectors in return for lenient audits of his companies, faces a new court hearing later this month, accused of illegally channeling funds to politicians.
